title: Electorate of Hanover
capsule: The Electorate of Brunswick-Lüneburg, commonly called Hanover, was created in 1692 when Emperor Leopold I elevated Duke Ernest Augustus to the dignity of prince-elector, consolidating the Welf holdings in north-western Germany. Its defining constitutional moment came in 1714 when Elector George Louis inherited the British throne as George I, inaugurating a personal union with Great Britain that lasted until 1837. French forces occupied the electorate in 1803 following the Peace of Lunéville, briefly incorporating it into the Kingdom of Westphalia, before its restoration and elevation to a kingdom at the Congress of Vienna in 1814.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The electorate's territory is well-documented through Holy Roman Empire records and British parliamentary sources; boundaries are reliably attested from 1692 onward.
